# 解深密經

**ID:** T0676
**Volume:** T16
**Category:** 經集部類
**Original Category:** 經集部
**Byline:** 唐 玄奘譯
**Dynasty:** 唐
**Date:** 647
**Juans:** 5
**CBETA:** https://cbetaonline.dila.edu.tw/zh/T0676

## Contributors
- 玄奘 (A000294)

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

T676 in five fascicles is [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98)'s definitive Chinese rendering of the *Saṃdhinirmocana-sūtra* and the textual basis of all subsequent East-Asian Yogācāra (Fǎxiàng 法相 / Cí'ēn 慈恩) exegesis. Translated at Hóngfúsì 弘福寺 in Cháng'ān in **Zhēnguān 21 (647 CE)**, two years after [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98)'s return from India in 645. The opening colophon reads "大唐三藏法師玄奘奉詔譯" ("translated by imperial decree by Tripiṭaka-dharma-master Xuánzàng of the Great Táng"). It is the single most important sūtra source for the Yogācāra-school *vijñapti-mātra* doctrine in China.

**Abstract**

[玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98)'s 647 translation of the *Saṃdhinirmocana* is one of the four complete or partial Chinese versions of this Yogācāra root-sūtra preserved in the Chinese canon: it is the latest ([KR6i0352](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0352) / T675 by [Bodhiruci](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%8F%A9%E6%8F%90%E6%B5%81%E6%94%AF) in 514 is older and complete; [KR6i0355](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0355) / T677 by [Paramārtha](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9C%9F%E8%AB%A6) in 557 covers only chapter 2; [KR6i0356](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0356) / T678 and [KR6i0357](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0357) / T679 by [Guṇabhadra](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B1%82%E9%82%A3%E8%B7%8B%E9%99%80%E7%BE%85) preserve only chapter 7 and chapter 8 respectively as separate "extracts"), and is universally recognised as the most accurate and stylistically polished. Its chapter division differs from the Bodhiruci version (eight chapters vs. eleven, with several of the bodhisattva-questioner chapters consolidated). The doctrinal armature — *ālayavijñāna* 阿賴耶識 (called by [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98) *ādānashí* 阿陀那識 in the third chapter, "Mind, Manas, and Consciousness"), the three self-natures (*parikalpita* 遍計所執 / *paratantra* 依他起 / *pariniṣpanna* 圓成實), and the three turnings of the wheel of dharma (三轉法輪) — is the standard scriptural ground for the East-Asian Yogācāra tradition. [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98)'s disciple [Wǒnch'ǔk / Yuáncè](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%9C%93%E6%B8%AC) (613–696) wrote the most influential medieval commentary, the *[Jiě shēnmì jīng shū 解深密經疏](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0354)* / X369 in ten fascicles (only fascicles 1–8 and partial fascicle 10 transmitted in Chinese; the whole work survives in Tibetan translation as *Dgongs pa nges par 'grel pa'i mdo'i rgya cher 'grel pa*).
